cases.note: check_portability.py needs a shell, and official sources cannot be re-read without network.

assertions.assertion: Reads the design and the plan before writing.
assertions.quote: Facts marked inspected were read in `claims/agent.py` and `claims/tools.py`; the rest is design-only.
assertions.reason: The document cites design IDs, plan goals and the scope gate, showing both design and plan were read before writing.

assertions.assertion: Writes docs/portability/claims.md from the skill's template with every required section.
assertions.reason: The 15 template sections cannot be confirmed: the document lacks an explicit section for design hash or evidence, and the final answer admits the hash was not recorded and the checker was not run.

assertions.assertion: Classifies each component as shared logic, a replaceable adapter, provider-specific by choice or an expensive dependency, citing the design's IDs.
assertions.quote: | Memory Bank and `PreloadMemoryTool` | D1, C2, R2 | expensive dependency |
assertions.reason: Every component is classified into one of the four classes with design IDs cited.

assertions.assertion: Assesses cloud, agent framework, model, service and deployment portability separately, each assessed or marked not a concern with a reason.
assertions.quote: | Deployment | Not a concern: one Cloud Run container behind the existing load balancer, no Agent Runtime features used (D6), so the image rehosts. |
assertions.reason: All five dimensions are covered, each either assessed or marked not a concern with a reason.

assertions.assertion: Compares the AWS and Azure alternatives and a small set of agent frameworks, with ADK first, citing official sources with their read dates.
assertions.quote: No web access was available in this session, so no source was re-verified. Each URL below is taken from the skill's reference notes, which record the read date shown.
assertions.reason: The document compares AWS, Azure and LangGraph with ADK as the baseline column, citing official sources with a 2026-10-26 read date.

assertions.assertion: Gives relative effort as small, medium, large, very large or unknown with stated drivers, sizing by the largest driver, and invents no hours, prices or dates.
assertions.quote: | Whole-system move to AWS | very large | Model, memory, retrieval, data and identity all change together; needs its own plan |
assertions.reason: Effort uses the allowed scale with stated drivers, sized by the combined drivers, and no hours, prices or dates are invented.

assertions.assertion: Runs check_portability.py with --design and --plan and fixes its errors before finishing.
assertions.reason: The checker was named with --design and --plan but not run, and the answer says so; the rubric note allows credit for naming it and saying it was not run, yet the assertion requires running and fixing errors, and the answer itself calls this undone.

assertions.assertion: Leaves the design and every other goal unchanged and writes no application code, Terraform, IAM policy or Kubernetes manifest.
assertions.quote: Status left at `ready`: it becomes `verified_local` only when the checker passes and the design hash matches.
assertions.reason: Only docs/portability/claims.md and the G07 ticket's Evidence section were changed; no code, Terraform, IAM or manifests were written.

cases.note: The deck check needs a shell; the default agent tools leave it out.

assertions.assertion: Opens with the decision requested and the result against the pre-agreed success criteria, taking every number from the plan's recorded evidence and citing the goal or acceptance ID under each claim.
assertions.quote: Three of four agreed criteria met. Refunds unproven. Spend £386.
assertions.reason: The deck opens with the result against S1-S4 and cites M/G IDs under each slide; derived figures (7.7%, 2.5-7.0%, £0.91) are labelled as the agent's own estimates, though they add numbers beyond the record.

assertions.assertion: States the two not-run acceptance cases and the open delegation decision as limits on the slides themselves rather than omitting them, and labels any projected production benefit as a hypothesis.
assertions.quote: Not run: shopper pointed to checkout if the delivery service is down (G02/A3).
assertions.reason: Both not-run cases and the open D6 decision appear on slides, and value in pounds and production cost are stated as not measured rather than projected.

assertions.assertion: Writes a stage-appropriate outline (criteria results, what was learned, production scope, cost, risks, the ask), the spoken narrative and a question list for a business audience, and keeps architecture detail for the technical version.
assertions.quote: Expected questions and where the record answers them
assertions.reason: The deck has criteria, learned, scope, cost, risks and ask slides, with spoken notes and a question slide, and leaves technical detail to a separate version.

assertions.assertion: Runs or describes the deck check so that every slide carries an evidence citation, and produces a one-page decision memo with the decision, owners and the date.
assertions.quote: The deck check hasn't been run. The slide and notes word budgets and the spoken-time estimate are unverified, so please run `check_deck.py` before using the deck.
assertions.reason: It names the checker and says it was not run, every slide has an Evidence line, and the memo carries the decision, owner and a date marked to be confirmed because none is recorded.

assertions.assertion: Does not modify application code, rerun evaluations or invent a demo result to fill a gap in evidence.
assertions.quote: No demo: none is recorded, so the deck says so and shows the measured results instead.
assertions.reason: Only presentation files were written under docs/presentations, with no code changes, no reruns and no invented demo.

cases.note: check_value_report.py needs a shell; the default agent tools leave it out.

assertions.assertion: Reads references/value-report.md and writes one page from assets/value-report-template.md, not a deck.
assertions.reason: Both the reference and the template were read, and a single-page markdown report was written (stated as 'One page for the sponsor'), not a deck.

assertions.assertion: Cites an M or I record for every figure and keeps estimates on lines opening with Estimate.
assertions.quote: We estimate this by dividing £512 by 1,184. Cost per accepted-unchanged draft (about 817 drafts, 69% of 1,184) would be about £0.63; we estimate this
assertions.reason: Estimates appear on lines that do not open with Estimate (the Actual line), and some figures cite the brief rather than an M or I record, so the convention is not followed throughout.

assertions.assertion: Runs scripts/check_value_report.py and reports the missing baseline and the stale August window rather than hiding them.
assertions.quote: I couldn't run `check_value_report.py` because this session has no shell tool.
assertions.reason: The checker was not run; the report did disclose the unmeasured September counter-metric and the August-only M3 window, but the assertion requires running the checker, and the missing M2 baseline field was not named.

assertions.assertion: Ends with a stop, continue or scale call naming the brief's decider and the figure or threshold it rests on.
assertions.quote: Helen Okafor decides by 2026-11-04 (assumed; see questions). Continue is recommended: the stop threshold did not fire (M2)
assertions.reason: The call is continue, names Helen Okafor as decider, rests on M2 13 minutes against the 15-minute threshold, and avoids a scale call.
